newsitem.title: FRANCE: FOCUS-France says it will meet EMU deficit goal.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-France says it will meet EMU deficit goal.

text.p: The French government said on Wednesday it would hit crucial deficit targets this year to qualify for European monetary union after announcing it slightly overshot its goal for 1996.
"I confirm that France will keep to its objective of limiting its deficits to three percent of GDP," Finance Minister Jean Arthuis told reporters.
Earlier, Arthuis said France's 1996 budget deficit would be equal to 4.1 percent of gross domestic product (GDP), just above its aim of reducing the deficit to four percent.
Arthuis said the overshoot did not worry him.
"It is a slippage of 0.1 percentage point and there is nothing in that to worry about. We kept our commitment" he said.

The Maastrict treaty - which sets goals on interest and exchange rates, inflation and public budgets -- calls for European nations to have deficits of no more than three percent of GDP in 1997 to qualify to take part in the single currency.
The single currency is due to go into effect on January 1, 1999.
France, suffering from weak economic growth that hit tax revenues, has been accused by critics of using "creative accounting" to reach its deficit targets.
Arthuis said economic growth for 1996 would be in line with the government's forecast of 1.3 percent. The government is targeting growth of 2.3 percent for 1997.
The 1996 budget deficit would total 295.4 billion francs ($51.9 billion), compared to the government's initial target of 287.8 billion, Arthuis said.
The figure is 28 billion francs lower than the 1995 deficit "despite a difficult macroeconomic context," he said. ($ = 5.697 French Francs)
